args.boundaryMapMarkdown:
## Boundary Map

### S01 → S02, S03, S05
Produces:
- Rust DLL with C ABI exports
- P/Invoke declarations in C#
- SoftwareBitmap conversion function
- Basic error handling at interop boundary

Consumes:
- nothing (first slice)

### S02 → S03, S05, S06, S07, S08, S09
Produces:
- Capture engine foundation (full screen, current monitor modes)
- Preview window with Image control
- Capture workflow orchestration
- Performance measurement infrastructure

Consumes from S01:
- Rust DLL with capture functions
- P/Invoke interop layer
- SoftwareBitmap conversion

### S03 → S07, S08
Produces:
- Active window capture mode
- Window under cursor capture mode
- Window decoration handling logic

Consumes from S01, S02:
- Rust capture engine
- Preview window
- Interop layer

### S04 → S05
Produces:
- WinUI overlay window pattern
- Rectangle drawing and manipulation primitives
- Keyboard event handling for region adjustments

Consumes from S02:
- Preview window patterns
- Basic WinUI setup

### S05 → S07
Produces:
- Rectangular region capture mode
- Region selector UI (draw, move, resize, confirm)
- Region coordinate passing to capture engine

Consumes from S01, S02, S04:
- Rust capture engine
- Preview window
- Overlay window patterns

### S06
Produces:
- Delayed capture workflow
- Countdown indicator UI
- Timer management

Consumes from S02:
- Capture engine
- Preview window

### S07 → S10
Produces:
- Save to file functionality
- Clipboard copy functionality
- Image file encoding (PNG)
- Filename template expansion

Consumes from S02, S03, S05:
- Capture engine and all modes
- Preview window
- SoftwareBitmap source

### S08
Produces:
- Global hotkey registration
- Hotkey message handling
- Hotkey-to-capture routing

Consumes from S02:
- Capture engine
- Preview window

### S09
Produces:
- Command-line argument parser
- CLI capture workflow
- Help and usage display

Consumes from S02:
- Capture engine
- All capture modes

### S10
Produces:
- Configuration file I/O (JSON)
- Settings model and persistence
- Config loading on startup

Consumes from S07:
- Save location and filename template logic
definitionOfDone: All slice deliverables complete and verified
Save to file with templates works
Performance thresholds met (<50ms capture, <30ms display, <1s startup)

keyRisks.risk: P/Invoke performance overhead at Rust↔C# boundary
WGC API limitations for window capture edge cases
keyRisks.whyItMatters: May cause window modes to fail unexpectedly

keyRisks.risk: WinUI 3 overlay window performance for region selector
keyRisks.whyItMatters: Selector must feel responsive or UX suffers

keyRisks.risk: Global hotkey conflicts with system or other apps
keyRisks.whyItMatters: Hotkeys may not register or work reliably

keyRisks.risk: Multi-monitor edge cases with different DPI scales

proofStrategy.whatWillBeProven: Rust↔C# interop round-trip time measured, image data flow verified
Core capture modes work end-to-end, edge cases identified
Selector overlay is responsive, rectangle operations feel smooth
All four Print Screen variants register and fire correctly
Window capture works correctly across multiple monitors with different DPI

args.requirementCoverage: Covers: R001 (5 capture modes), R002 (preview), R003 (region selector), R004 (delayed capture), R005 (save to file), R006 (copy to clipboard), R007 (hotkeys), R008 (CLI), R009 (multi-monitor), R010 (config), R011 (performance). Partially covers: None. Leaves for later: R020-R023. Orphan risks: None.

slices.demo: Simple Rust DLL with WGC capture called from C#, proves P/Invoke and image data flow works
slices.goal: Validate that Rust+WGC+P/Invoke architecture works before building full application. Prove image data can flow from Rust to WinUI 3 efficiently.
slices.integrationClosure: Rust and C# communicate successfully, WGC API accessible from Rust
slices.observabilityImpact: Add logging at interop boundary, measure and log round-trip times
slices.proofLevel: Contract proof: Interop works, image data flows
slices.successCriteria:
- Rust DLL compiles successfully
- C# loads Rust DLL
- P/Invoke calls execute without errors
- WGC captures full screen
- SoftwareBitmap created from Rust data
- Image displays in WinUI 3 Image control
- Round-trip time measured (<50ms target)
slices.title: Spike - Core Capture Validation

slices.demo: Can capture and display full screen and current monitor screenshots in preview window
slices.goal: Build the foundation: Rust capture engine with full screen and current monitor modes, WinUI 3 preview window, basic error handling.
slices.integrationClosure: Rust capture engine integrated with WinUI 3 UI, preview workflow complete
slices.observabilityImpact: Log capture start/end, measure and log latencies, log errors with context
slices.proofLevel: Integration proof: End-to-end capture and display
slices.successCriteria:
- Full screen capture (all monitors) works
- Current screen capture (monitor under cursor) works
- Preview window displays captured screenshots
- Display latency <30ms verified
- App startup <1s verified
- Basic error handling in place
- SoftwareBitmap creation efficient
slices.title: Foundation and Core Capture

slices.demo: Can capture active window and window under cursor correctly
slices.goal: Add active window and window under cursor capture modes to the foundation.
slices.integrationClosure: Window capture modes integrated with foundation, accessible from all entry points
slices.observabilityImpact: Log window detection, log capture boundaries, log any WGC window-specific errors
slices.proofLevel: Integration proof: Window capture works end-to-end
slices.successCriteria:
- Active window capture works correctly
- Window under cursor capture works correctly
- Multi-monitor window capture verified
- Window decorations handled correctly
- Both modes accessible from UI and CLI
slices.title: Window Capture Modes

slices.demo: Minimal WinUI overlay window with rectangle drawing, proves selector UI approach
slices.goal: Validate that WinUI 3 can create a responsive overlay window for rectangular region selection. Prove drawing, moving, resizing rectangles works.
slices.integrationClosure: WinUI overlay pattern proven, rectangle operations performant
slices.observabilityImpact: Log overlay window lifecycle, log rectangle coordinates, log keyboard events
slices.proofLevel: Contract proof: Overlay window and rectangle manipulation work
slices.successCriteria:
- WinUI overlay window displays over desktop
- Mouse drag draws rectangle visual
- Rectangle can be moved
- Rectangle can be resized
- Keyboard arrow keys work (normal, Shift+slow, Alt+resize)
- Confirmed region coordinates accessible
slices.title: Spike - Rectangular Region Selector Validation

slices.demo: Can draw, move, resize, and confirm rectangular screen region for capture
slices.goal: Build complete rectangular region selector with capture integration. All draw, move, resize, confirm operations must work.
slices.integrationClosure: Region selector passes coordinates to Rust capture engine, captures selected area
slices.observabilityImpact: Log all selector operations, log final region coordinates, log capture trigger
slices.proofLevel: Integration proof: Region selector integrates with capture engine
slices.successCriteria:
- Draw rectangle with mouse drag works
- Move rectangle with mouse and keyboard works
- Resize rectangle with mouse and keyboard works
- Double-click confirms selection
- Enter key confirms selection
- Arrow keys: normal move, Shift+slow move, Alt+resize
- Region persists during capture operation
- Works across multiple monitors
slices.title: Rectangular Region Selector

slices.demo: Can set delay seconds, see countdown indicator, capture triggers after delay
slices.goal: Add delayed capture functionality with visible countdown. Users can set delay and cancel if needed.
slices.integrationClosure: Delayed capture workflow integrated with all capture modes
slices.observabilityImpact: Log delay start, countdown tick, cancel, capture trigger
slices.proofLevel: Contract proof: Timer and countdown work
slices.successCriteria:
- Configurable delay (0-60 seconds) works
- Countdown indicator visible in window title
- Task manager button shows progress bar
- Cancel button appears during countdown
- Cancel stops countdown and returns to ready state
- Capture triggers automatically after delay completes
- Works for all capture modes
slices.title: Delayed Capture

slices.demo: Can save screenshots to configurable location with filename templates, copy to clipboard
slices.goal: Add save to file and copy to clipboard functionality. Include filename template expansion.
slices.integrationClosure: Export functionality integrated with all capture modes, works with preview window
slices.observabilityImpact: Log save operations, log errors, measure save times
slices.proofLevel: Integration proof: Save and copy work with captured images
slices.successCriteria:
- Save to file works (PNG format)
- Configurable save location works
- Filename template with placeholders works
- Placeholders: <dd>, <hh>, <MM>, <ss>, <title>, <yyyy>, <#>, <mm>, <yy>
- Copy to clipboard works
- File save <100ms verified
- Error handling for permissions/disk full/invalid path
slices.title: Export and Clipboard

slices.demo: Can trigger captures via Print Screen, Meta+Print, Shift+Print, Meta+Shift+Print
slices.goal: Register and handle global keyboard shortcuts for all capture modes. Hotkeys must work even when app is minimized.
slices.integrationClosure: Global hotkeys integrated with capture engine and preview window
slices.observabilityImpact: Log hotkey registration, log hotkey triggers, log conflicts
slices.proofLevel: Integration proof: Hotkeys trigger captures correctly
slices.successCriteria:
- Print Screen triggers full screen capture
- Meta+Print triggers active window capture
- Shift+Print triggers full desktop capture
- Meta+Shift+Print triggers rectangular region capture
- Hotkeys work when app is minimized
- Hotkeys work when app is focused
- Hotkey registration on startup
- Hotkey unregistration on shutdown
- Handle hotkey conflicts gracefully
slices.title: Global Hotkeys

slices.demo: Can capture from command line without showing UI
slices.goal: Build CLI that can trigger all capture modes without showing the UI window. Support filename and location arguments.
slices.integrationClosure: CLI integrated with Rust capture engine, bypasses UI
slices.observabilityImpact: Log CLI arguments, log capture start/end, log errors to stderr
slices.proofLevel: Contract proof: CLI triggers captures correctly
slices.successCriteria:
- CLI accepts capture mode arguments
- CLI captures without showing UI
- CLI supports filename argument
- CLI supports location argument
- Help command displays usage
- Exit codes indicate success (0) or failure (non-zero)
- Error messages printed to stderr
- All 5 capture modes accessible via CLI
slices.title: Command-Line Interface

slices.demo: Settings (save location, filename template) persist across sessions
slices.goal: Add configuration persistence. User settings save to JSON file in AppData and load on startup.
slices.integrationClosure: Configuration integrated with save functionality, loads on app startup
slices.observabilityImpact: Log config load/save, log errors, log reset to defaults
slices.proofLevel: Contract proof: Config persists and loads
slices.successCriteria:
- Save location persists across sessions
- Filename template persists across sessions
- JSON file written to %APPDATA%\respectacle\
- JSON file read on startup
- Corrupted config resets to defaults
- Corrupted config backed up before reset
- Config changes take effect immediately
- Invalid save path handled gracefully
slices.title: Configuration

successCriteria: All 5 capture modes work end-to-end (full screen, current screen, rectangular region, active window, window under cursor)
Preview window displays captured screenshots correctly
Rectangular region selector UI works (draw, move, resize, confirm)
Delayed capture with countdown indicator works
Save to file works with configurable location and filename templates
Command-line interface works for all capture modes
Multi-monitor support verified on actual multi-monitor setup
All performance thresholds met (capture <50ms, display <30ms, startup <1s)
args.title: Core Capture
args.verificationContract: Performance thresholds verified: capture <50ms (Rust→C# image available), display <30ms (preview rendered), startup <1s (app ready). Multi-monitor capture verified on actual setup. All 5 modes produce valid SoftwareBitmap. Spikes validate interop and selector before main implementation.
args.verificationIntegration: Rust DLL loads in C# process, P/Invoke calls succeed, captured images display in WinUI 3 Image control. Global hotkeys registered and fire even when app minimized. CLI captures without showing UI. Configuration persists across app restarts.
args.verificationOperational: App launches within 1s, hotkeys work on running or newly-started app, captures complete within 80ms total (trigger→display), app handles rapid repeated captures without degradation. Multi-monitor setups work correctly.
args.verificationUat: User can take all 5 types of screenshots, preview them, save with custom filenames, copy to clipboard, use Print Screen shortcuts, and run CLI commands. Settings persist. Performance feels instant.
args.vision: Build a high-performance screenshot capture application with Rust engine and WinUI 3 UI. Capture the entire desktop, individual monitors, active windows, windows under cursor, or rectangular regions. Preview, save, copy to clipboard, trigger via global hotkeys or CLI. All with near-instant performance.
